summary.headline: Sportking expects top line up 7-10% and margins to expand 15-20% QoQ over next three quarters on higher yarn prices and a long sales book.
summary.overview: Management described a resilient Q4 FY26 with revenue broadly stable and profitability improved, driven by better yarn realisation and stronger cotton yarn demand. Demand was attributed to China's resurgence as a cotton yarn importer, Bangladesh recovery, and a stronger rupee-driven competitiveness shift for Indian spinning. Management said spreads are at roughly three-year highs and expects margins to expand over the next two to three quarters, with the 150,000-spindle greenfield project slated for commercial operations in Q3 FY27. Acquisitions of a majority stake in Marvel Dyers and Processors and the Sobhagia Sales manufacturing facilities were approved, with closure targeted within the calendar year.

financial_highlights.value: Broadly stable (no figure stated on call)

financial_highlights.change: Expected to reverse in Q1 if rupee does not depreciate further
Management estimate for current/coming financial year

segments.name: Cotton yarn (core)
segments.commentary: Demand robust across segments for last 2-3 months; yarn prices moved from about USD2.70-2.80/kg average last quarter to near USD3.30 now. Export book covers about 90 days, with the current quarter largely sold.

segments.name: Acquired entities (Marvel Dyers and Processors; Sobhagia Sales facilities)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue about INR200 crores (7-8% of turnover). Group companies expected to be flattish in FY26 and grow 15-20% in FY27 after reengineering, versus management's earlier 20-25% framing.

guidance_outlook: Top line expected to rise 7-10% over the next three quarters on higher yarn prices; no volume growth as plant runs at 95-96% optimum utilisation.

Quarter-on-quarter margin expansion targeted at least 15-20% over the next two to three quarters, supported by spreads and the long sales book; management said it would be disappointed not to deliver 15%+ margins in H1 but declined to give formal guidance.

Greenfield 150,000-spindle expansion (approx. INR1,000 crores) expected to start commercial operations in Q3 FY27, with a little contribution in Q3 and a more substantial contribution from Q4 and fully from FY28.
40 MW solar to commence by end-May 2026, saving INR14-15 crores annually.
Acquisitions expected to close within the current calendar year at the latest; bigger downstream plans to be shared after 6-9 months of integration.
EU and UK FTAs expected to be effective by end of FY27 (UK in 2-3 months, EU in about 6 months per management's read of government sources).
capex_capacity: Greenfield expansion of approximately INR1,000 crores adds about 150,000 spindles; land acquired, machinery advances released, construction on schedule, commercial operations targeted Q3 FY27 in Odisha.
Ramp-up: first output about 2 months after commissioning, then about 15-16% of capacity added each month; 97-98% utilisation expected about 6 months after commissioning.

40 MW solar plant to commence by end-May 2026 under Punjab policy, supplying about 7 crore units per year at about INR3.70/unit, saving about INR2/unit (INR14-15 crores annually). Management said no further ground-mounted solar planned in Odisha, only possible small rooftop solar.

Acquisition of majority stake in Marvel Dyers and Processors Pvt Ltd approved by Board; acquisition of manufacturing facilities of Sobhagia Sales Pvt Ltd on slump-sale basis and land and building on lease basis, subject to definitive agreements and approvals.
Current plant running at about 95-96% of optimum capacity.
demand_pricing: China's share of Indian cotton yarn exports rose from about 7-8% to roughly 25-30% per management; Sportking's China exports rose from about 2-3% to about 10-12% of its exports in the last quarter.
Bangladesh remains Sportking's largest export market; domestic demand has picked up since March after the US tariff removal.
Cotton yarn spread about USD1.00/kg (skein cost vs. yarn price) versus USD0.65-0.70 over the last couple of years; cotton spreads at about 3-year highs.
Cotton covered for 3-6 months; management did not disclose coverage levels, saying all good mills cover most of the season's cotton by end-March.

CCI bought 106 lakh bales of a projected 310 lakh bale crop (about 33-34%), which management says lifts market prices toward MSP at harvest; government import-duty relief on cotton awaited within a couple of months.
Export mix roughly 50% international, plus or minus 5%, which management expects to stay in this range with FTAs.

qa_highlights.question: How will new capacity ramp, and why are spreads rising and sustainable for 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads supported by a 90-day export book already largely sold for the current quarter and cotton covered for 3-6 months. New greenfield capacity is on timeline, with 97-98% utilisation about 6 months after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Is China a durable demand source given historical volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged volatility but said Chinese domestic demand has turned after 4-5 years of weakness and that China now needs to import cotton given peaking domestic production and high cotton duties.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to margins once new-crop cotton prices fall or rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current spreads are among the best of the last 3 years even at today's cotton prices; April-September is seasonally weak and October-March is seasonally stronger. No crystal ball on pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for H1 FY27 and quarter-on-quarter trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin expansion of at least 15-20% over the next 2-3 quarters, citing higher yarn prices (USD3.30 vs USD2.70-2.80) and the long sales book. It declined to give formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the acquisitions and synergies on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired entities are about 7-8% of turnover (about INR200 crores). Immediate margin impact is small; they serve as labs for downstream expansion. Closure expected this calendar year at the latest.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin and the forex hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Better spreads and robust demand drove margin; some small provisions held it back. The forex loss was a notional mark-to-market on unshipped and unreceived items at the all-time-high dollar on 31 March, expected to reverse if the rupee does not weaken further. Management said it books sales the same day and holds no open risk.

risks_watch: Chinese demand volatility; management acknowledged China has been a volatile market.
New-crop cotton prices and procurement cost in October onward could compress spreads; no guidance given on post-H1 margins.
Greenfield project timeline (Q3 FY27 start) and ramp-up pace; construction risk.
Pending duty decision on cotton imports; CCI procurement share (about 33-34%) influences domestic prices.
Forex mark-to-market swings on open export and import items; Q4 contained a notional charge.
Integration and value addition of acquired downstream businesses; long-term plans to be disclosed after 6-9 months.
Macro risk from multiple wars and higher inflation forecasts, per management.
Group company revenue fell over FY23-FY25; FY26 expected flat, growth of 15-20% in FY27 needs delivery.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and spreads, with forward targets stated firmly (7-10% revenue growth, 15-20% QoQ margin expansion). Evasive on specifics: declined to disclose cotton coverage levels, gave no formal margin guidance, and gave no Q4 figures beyond a 13% EBITDA margin cited by an analyst.

So we expect top line to increase by 7% to 10% in the next three quarters because of the higher prices.
So either you modernize or you shut down.

growth.why: Management guides top line up 7-10% over the next three quarters (FY27 expectation INR2,700-2,800 crores) on higher yarn prices and a ~90-day export book, with no volume growth as the plant runs at 95-96%; the 150,000-spindle Odisha expansion (~INR1,000 crores) targets Q3 FY27 start, so volume growth is only partly backed by specific capacity and orders.
